findings.title: Test helpers return `object`, forcing pervasive `# type: ignore` in strict-checked tests
findings.description: `scripted_session`, `sdk_text`, `sdk_result`, `typed_config` and the other new helpers are annotated as returning `object`. Every caller then needs `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` (`tests/pipeline/test_sdk_session.py` has dozens). The Python rules require strict pyright on test code and say bugs in tests can mask bugs in code. `scripted_session` should return `SDKExecutionSession`. The message builders should return the SDK message types or `Any`. `typed_config` should return a `Callable`. The `_ledger_after` helper in `test_sdk_session.py` has the same problem. Proper return types would remove most of the ignores.

findings.title: Timing-based tests rely on wall-clock sleeps
findings.description: The idle-timeout tests patch the timeout to 0.05s and script a 0.15s sleep. `test_slow_foreground_turn_has_no_timer` sleeps 0.1s. The 3x margin can fail on a loaded CI box. Making the timeout much smaller than the sleep (for example 0.01s against 0.5s), or driving the clock deterministically, would remove the flake risk.

findings.title: Pyright suppression at the options boundary in `open_pipeline_session`
findings.description: `SdkSettings.setting_sources` is typed `list[str]`, while the SDK expects a list of literals. The mismatch is hidden with `# pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]`. `provider.py` handles the same boundary with `# type: ignore[arg-type]`. Typing `SdkSettings` with the SDK's `SettingSource` literal, or casting once inside `settings.py`, would fix this in one place instead of at every caller.

findings.title: Config is read from different directories on the one-shot and session paths
findings.description: `one_shot_dispatch_with_telemetry` resolves `pipeline.user_settings` and `pipeline.auto_memory` from the caller's `cwd`. The SDK agent itself is spawned with `cwd=None`, so the CLI runs in the process cwd. `open_pipeline_session` reads the same keys from `Path.cwd()`. If a caller passes a `cwd`, one-shot dispatch can pick up a different project's config than the process the CLI runs in, and than the session path would. Using one rule for both paths (and documenting it) would avoid surprising per-project overrides.

findings.title: Comment points to a table that is no longer adjacent
findings.description: The `SystemPromptMode` docstring says "the four rows of the table above". The table is a comment on `AgentConfig.use_default_system_prompt`, about 40 lines earlier and in a different class. The `SystemPromptMode` docstring should name that field instead. Separately, `describe_*` helpers that render SDK-specific settings now sit in `core/models.py`. That is a mild layering smell, and they would sit better next to `providers/sdk/settings.py`.

findings.title: Error-path handling in the new session loop is sound
findings.description: Both broad `except Exception` blocks follow the project rules. `_reconnect` logs with `logger.exception`, records `unusable_reason` and re-raises. `_stop_background` has a justified inline comment and logs per task id. A stream that ends with agents still tracked raises instead of returning partial text. Tests cover each of these paths.
